sources.title: G. B. Mbeng, A. Russomanno, and G. E. Santoro, The quantum Ising chain for beginners, SciPost Physics Lecture Notes submission, arXiv:2009.09208v2 (19 June 2024)
sources.locator: Complete 83-page v2 manuscript; §3.1.1, Eqs. (79)–(80), printed pp.20–21; §6.2, Eqs. (149)–(165), printed pp.38–41.

contents.name: Open-boundary Majorana diagonalization and the bond-to-Majorana relation

source_review.read_extent: Read the OBC quadratic matrix and its two zero eigenvalues for the four-site illustration, the paired mode combinations, the Majorana definitions and anticommutators, the neighboring-bond identity, and the zero-mode discussion through Eq. (165), printed pp.38–41.
source_review.supports: The open-chain quadratic-Majorana method and the fact that Ising bonds pair neighboring Majorana operators.
source_review.limitations: The worked matrix is L=4 and the phase discussion assumes ordered positive couplings. The assigned proof establishes the all-N matrix identity and trace directly for arbitrary real h,J; it does not import a boundary-mode classification.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §3.1.1 reasoning through Eqs. (79)–(80), including the parity-sector momentum caveat and its thermodynamic-limit qualification.
source_review.supports: The positive dispersion has a lower edge that closes at the uniform-chain critical coupling in the source's h>0, J>0 convention.
source_review.limitations: The source result is a periodic-spin-chain excitation gap in the positive-coupling convention. The assigned item proves the spectrum of a separately defined infinite one-particle convolution operator for all real h,J, including the momentum shift when hJ<0.

contents.name: Topological boundary-mode and infinite-spin ground-state conclusions after Eq. (165)
contents.reason: The assigned conclusions concern the finite open quadratic Hamiltonian and the spectrum of the infinite one-particle operator; they do not assert a topological invariant, infinite-volume spin-ground-state uniqueness, or a thermodynamic singularity.

sources.title: Pieter Claeys, Quench dynamics in the Transverse Field Ising Model, Many-body Quantum Dynamics @ TU Dresden lecture notes

contents.name: Jordan–Wigner string, CAR signs, and quadratic Ising Hamiltonian, Eqs. (49)–(61)

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete derivation from the Pauli raising/lowering matrices through the string operators, their cross-site sign check, the inverse spin formula, and the cancellation of strings in the nearest-neighbor TFIM Hamiltonian.
source_review.supports: The need for ordered nonlocal Z strings to convert commuting spin operators into anticommuting fermionic operators, and the local quadratic form after adjacent strings cancel.
source_review.limitations: The note's displayed Hamiltonian has a +h sigma-z term and is written with periodic indexing before its parity-sector boundary discussion. The assigned finite open-chain signs and endpoint convention are computed locally from explicit matrices.

contents.name: Bogoliubov dispersion and occupation spectrum, Eqs. (65)–(68)

source_review.read_extent: Read the diagonalizing transformation, the formula epsilon_h(k)=2 sqrt(J^2+h^2-2Jh cos k), the mode occupation energies, and the momentum quantization that follows from the fermion-parity boundary conditions.
source_review.supports: The two-component Fourier symbol's positive dispersion and the finite-mode energy normalization.
source_review.limitations: The source uses periodic finite chains with parity-dependent momenta. The assigned proof uses an infinite two-site-cell convolution operator and proves its full spectrum by Fourier multiplication and approximate eigenvectors.

contents.name: Periodic-spin versus fermionic parity boundary conditions, Eqs. (62)–(63)

source_review.read_extent: Read the explicit even/odd fermion-parity boundary-condition split and the resulting discrete momentum grids.
source_review.supports: The warning that a periodic spin boundary cannot be silently treated as an ordinary periodic fermion boundary.
source_review.limitations: The assigned definition is open before Jordan–Wigner conversion, so its bond sum has no wraparound term and requires no parity-sector correction.
